newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stock fall unlikely to hurt capital spending -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Stock fall unlikely to hurt capital spending -- EPA.

text.p: The recent plunge in Tokyo stock prices is unlikely to have a negative impact on Japan's capital spending and private consumption, Economic Planning Agency Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told a news conference on Friday.

He said the Japanese economy was not expected to contract in the 1997/98 fiscal year, despite an expected slowdown in the first part of that fiscal year due to a planned increase in the national consumption tax to five percent from the current three percent on April 1.
"From the macro-economic point of view, the recent fall in stock prices is unlikely to affect capital spending or household spending," Nukaya said.

He also said the economy was likely to retain its firmness at least until the beginning of the next fiscal year, taking into account the strong outlook for machinery orders for the October to December period of last year.
The EPA announced on Thursday that machinery orders for the October to December period were expected to meet the official estimate of a 19.3 percent rise from the previous quarter.
"The economy may slow down at the start of the next fiscal year, but will go back into a recovery trend in the latter half without heading downward," he said.
